sense: for the sake of, for a purpose

terms.gloss: for the sake of; for (a purpose)
terms.grammar: the ablative of causa, placed after its genitive
evidence: Cic. Amic. 44: amīcōrum causā honesta faciāmus
terms.comment: With a person’s pronoun, the possessive: meā causā, tuā causā, for my sake, for yours. With a gerund it gives the purpose: lūdendī causā, for play. See purpose.

terms.grammar: the ablative of grātia, placed after its genitive
evidence: Quint. 1.1.26: irrītandae ad discendum īnfantiae grātiā
terms.comment: Less common than causā in Cicero; at home in set phrases such as exemplī grātiā, for example.

terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative, often of a gerund or gerundive
evidence: Varr. RR 1.54.2: legitur ad bibendum, ēligitur ad edendum
Liv. 21.54.8: ope ūllā ad arcendum frīgus adhibitā
terms.comment: What a thing is meant for: ad bibendum, for drinking.

terms.grammar: construction: the dative, often of a gerundive
terms.comment: After ūtilis, aptus and in set phrases.

phrases.latin: nūllus sūmptus est, et sī sūmptus esset, tamen valētūdinis causā experīrēs
phrases.english: it costs nothing; and even if it did, you would still try it for your health

phrases.latin: haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur, ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus, amīcōrum causā honesta faciāmus
phrases.english: let this be the first law of friendship: ask friends only for what is right, and do only what is right for friends’ sake

phrases.latin: Salūtis causā bene fit hominī injūria.
phrases.english: To hurt someone for the sake of his health is to do right.

phrases.latin: sublātum pedem ostendere mihi et porgere quasi opis petendae grātiā vīsus est
phrases.english: he seemed to lift his paw, show it to me and hold it out, as if to ask for help

phrases.latin: in vindēmiā dīligentis ūva nōn sōlum legitur sed etiam ēligitur; legitur ad bibendum, ēligitur ad edendum
phrases.english: at a careful man’s vintage the grapes are not only picked but picked over: picked for drinking, picked over for eating

phrases.latin: haec tibi sorte datur tergendīs spongia mēnsīs ūtilis, expressō cum levis imbre tumet
phrases.english: this sponge is your prize in the draw, useful for wiping tables when, squeezed dry, it swells up light
